### SPHERALYX AI — Project Summary

SPHERALYX AI is an interactive, AI-powered astronomy platform designed to explore the universe and investigate moving celestial objects using NASA's SPHEREx mission data.

We developed a platform that combines NASA/IPAC astronomical observations, Python-based machine learning, Google Gemini AI, and interactive 3D visualizations. Users can explore planetary systems, examine planets, comets, and asteroids, compare observations across multiple epochs, and investigate potential movement through astronomical imagery.

Our project addresses the **NASA Space Apps Challenge: Planet X and SPHEREx** by making the search for moving objects more accessible through visual exploration, image comparison, and AI-assisted interpretation. It clearly distinguishes simulated objects from real scientific observations and unverified candidates.

SPHERALYX AI is important because it transforms complex astronomical information into an engaging educational and exploratory experience, helping students, researchers, and space enthusiasts better understand how scientists investigate our universe.

SPHERALYX AI — Project Details

Project Overview

SPHERALYX AI is an AI-powered astronomical exploration platform designed to make space exploration more interactive, accessible, and scientifically engaging. Our project combines real astronomical data from NASA's SPHEREx mission, machine learning, interactive 3D simulations, and generative artificial intelligence to help users investigate celestial objects and understand how astronomers search for movement across the universe.

How Does It Work?

SPHERALYX AI connects to NASA/IPAC's Infrared Science Archive (IRSA), allowing users to search for SPHEREx observations, access astronomical data, and visualize scientific FITS images.

The platform supports multi-epoch analysis, enabling users to compare observations from different dates using World Coordinate System (WCS) alignment and image-difference techniques. These tools help highlight changes that may warrant further scientific investigation.

Our Python-based machine learning system uses RandomForest to demonstrate how moving objects can be classified and evaluated. Its current training and validation use synthetic datasets, while the real-data pipeline provides exploratory image analysis rather than confirmed astronomical discoveries.

The platform also features an interactive 3D Cosmic Explorer where users can navigate simulated planetary systems, observe orbital motion, select planets, comets, and asteroids, and examine their properties.

Google Gemini powers an integrated AI assistant that helps explain astronomical concepts, interpret available results, and guide users through the platform.

Technologies Used

Our project was developed using:

  • Python, FastAPI, and scikit-learn: Backend services, data processing, and machine learning.
  • Astropy, NumPy, and scientific image-processing techniques: FITS interpretation, astronomical coordinates, and multi-epoch comparisons.
  • JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and WebGL: Interactive astronomical visualization and responsive interfaces.
  • Google Gemini API: AI-powered explanations and contextual assistance.
  • NASA/IPAC IRSA and SPHEREx datasets: Access to authentic astronomical observations.
  • GitHub and Render: Version control, testing, deployment, and cloud hosting.

The platform is designed to operate through a web browser without requiring specialized hardware from users.

Innovation and Creativity

What makes SPHERALYX AI unique is its combination of scientific data exploration, interactive planetary simulations, and conversational artificial intelligence within a single platform.

Rather than simply displaying astronomical information, the system encourages users to interact with celestial objects, explore changes between observation epochs, and investigate potential movement.

The project also incorporates educational assessments of planetary characteristics and potential habitability within simulated environments, while clearly distinguishing hypothetical properties from verified scientific measurements.

Benefits and Expected Impact

SPHERALYX AI aims to make advanced astronomical concepts easier to understand for students, educators, researchers, and space enthusiasts.

By simplifying access to scientific observations and providing interactive explanations, the platform can encourage interest in astronomy, artificial intelligence, scientific programming, and data analysis.

Its long-term vision is to support educational exploration and the preliminary investigation of astronomical observations, helping more people participate in understanding how potential moving celestial objects are identified and studied.

Key Considerations

During development, our team prioritized scientific transparency, usability, accessibility, performance, and responsible AI integration.

We carefully distinguished simulated observations from authentic NASA data and avoided presenting preliminary movement hypotheses as confirmed planetary discoveries.

Our ultimate goal is to transform complex astronomical data into an accessible, intelligent, and engaging exploration experience that inspires the next generation of space explorers.
